findings.title: The goal (lamp and socket) is off-screen for nearly the whole job, and the marker has no off-screen indicator
findings.problem: At the home zoom of 17 (src/game.ts:397) the camera follows Pip closely. The lamp and socket at (7,-6) are out of frame at the start (shot 01), just after picking up the plug (shot 10), and after the first leg to (-5,-1) (shot 11). They only come into view in the last few metres of the drag (shot 13). The step-2 card says 'Drag the cable to the lamp's socket and plug it in', but a new player has no lamp in view. The bouncing marker (src/ui/objectives.ts:96-97, 119-120) is a world-space cone with no screen-edge arrow, so while the target is off-screen it gives no direction at all. Even in the survey (shot 02) and at max zoom (shot 07) the lamp is a thin dark-grey pole with a small shade in the far corner, against a cream wall. It is one of the lowest-contrast shapes in the room, while crates, bookshelves of saturated books and hazard-striped pillars shout louder. A first-time player has to guess, or find Tab, to learn where to go. That undercuts 'play by doing': the scene does not show the goal.
findings.fix: (1) Add a screen-edge pointer in ObjectivesHUD.update (src/ui/objectives.ts:118). Project `at` with view.camera. When it falls outside the viewport inset by 8%, show a 32 px outlined chevron clamped to the screen edge, pointing toward it. (2) Make the lamp read from across the room. In src/levels/decor.ts:89-92, raise the pole to 3.2 m and the shade radius to 0.55, paint the pole and base a saturated job colour instead of DMETAL/INK, and add an unlit 'dead bulb' halo ring (MeshBasic #ffe9a8, opacity 0.35) that pulses until lit. (3) Optionally run a 1.5 s intro camera glide in Game.begin from the lamp to Pip, or set the start yaw so the lamp is in the first frame.
findings.verify: Retake playground-play-10 and -11: the edge chevron is visible and points toward the lamp. In a squint test of a greyscale survey shot, the lamp is among the three highest-contrast shapes (DR-43).
findings.verify_reason: Checked shots 01, 10, 11 and 13: the lamp and socket at (7,-6) are out of frame at the home zoom until the last metres of the drag. In my own idle-hint start shot the lamp is also not visible. ObjectivesHUD.update (src/ui/objectives.ts:118-120) only positions a world-space cone, and nothing handles the target being off-screen. In the survey (shot 02) the lamp is findable (yellow shade plus teal ring, top right) but small. The core claim holds.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-playground-play-01-idle-hint.jpg (start framing at 0:36, lamp not in frame)

findings.title: There is no switch: 'Switch the lamp on' is E at a bare lamp pole, and the switch state is invisible
findings.problem: The playground's third step (src/ui/objectives.ts:26) and the concept it teaches ('a switch closes the loop', per research-docs) have no switch model. switchAt (7.55,-6.35) in src/levels/playground.ts:6 is exactly the lamp pole's position (src/levels/decor.ts:89, group at t.x+.55, t.z-.35), and decor builds no switch mesh (grep 'switch' in decor.ts finds nothing). The player presses E at a grey pole; the only feedback is 6 sparks and a click (src/game.ts:217). The marker points at mid-pole (shots 14, 39). The state is also invisible. Before power, E toggles switchedOn with the prompt 'Switch on (needs power first)', and the next E silently toggles it back off (g-misc log: sw true → false → true, with nothing visible changing). A player who presses E at the lamp while exploring can leave it ON and then win the moment they plug in, or leave it OFF and not know why the lamp stays dark. A switch that can't be seen can't teach 'open vs closed'.
findings.fix: Build a chunky wall-box toggle on the lamp pole at about 1.0 m in src/levels/decor.ts playground(): a 0.22×0.32×0.1 rbox housing, a 0.08×0.16 lever and an ink outline. Return it in Decor (e.g. decor.switch), and in Game.interact rotate the lever ±35° when switchedOn changes. Add a small indicator lamp on the box, dark when the loop is open and green only when connected && switchedOn. Point the step-3 marker at the box (switchAt y≈1.0). Optionally draw a short visible lead from the socket box up the pole to the switch, then to the bulb, so the series path reads.
findings.verify: Close shot at the lamp (zoom 9) before and after E. The lever position differs and a new viewer can say ON/OFF with the HUD hidden. Run the routes.spec playground test and confirm it still passes.
findings.verify_reason: decor.ts playground() builds no switch mesh (grep 'switch' in decor.ts finds nothing). The step-3 marker sits mid-pole beside the shade (my close shot 03). I reproduced the state bug: with no plug, E at (6.6,-5.9) shows 'Switch on (needs power first)' and toggles switchedOn true→false→true with no visible change. Then I dragged and plugged in with the switch already on, and the room was won at the instant of plug-in (won:true, electrical 'on'). Step 3 was skipped entirely, so the 'switch closes the loop' beat can be bypassed without the player ever seeing it.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-playground-play/v2.mjs b: E1 sw true, E2 false, E3 true; plugged with switch pre-on -> won true at t 10.63
src/game.ts:217 toggles switchedOn regardless of connected
findings.fix_correction: Also refuse the toggle before power, or keep the lever visibly ON so pre-switching is readable. For example, in Game.interact only allow switchedOn=true when connected, and otherwise play a dead click and leave it off. That way plug-in never wins without the step-3 beat, unless the lever is visibly up.

findings.title: The cyan 'route hint' dots flow on an open circuit, start from Pip rather than the plug, and run straight through crates and shelves
findings.problem: After 35 s without a connection, 40 glowing cyan dots stream from Pip toward the socket (src/game.ts:100, :446). Three problems. (a) Moving glowing dots are the game's language for current (the pulses on a live gold cable). Showing them on an open circuit, before the plug is in, teaches the 'electricity flows out to the device' misconception (DR-29, EXT M2). (b) They start at Pip's feet even during step 1, when Pip has not picked up the plug. In shot 33 Pip stands at spawn and the dots lead away from the reel, contradicting the card ('Pick up the reel's plug'). (c) The path is `detour(Pip, target, this.obstacles)`, and this.obstacles holds only the two pillars. So the dots cut straight through the crate stack (shot 33), the bookshelves and clutter (shot 37), a route the cable or Pip cannot actually take.
findings.fix: In src/game.ts:446, replace the flowing dots with a static or slowly blinking dashed floor line, or footprints, in a non-electric colour such as warm white #fff3d6 at opacity 0.6, so moving beads stay reserved for live current. Start it at the plug while !holdingPlug, and at Pip or the plug end once carrying. Route it with the same obstacle list the rope uses (pillars plus props of mass ≥3 near the path, as in simulateCable), or around the lane polyline the level declares (playground.ts:6 lanes[0]).
findings.verify: Advance 36 s idle and retake playground-play-33: the line starts at the plug, does not cross a crate or shelf, and nothing moves along it. Grep for flowing-bead effects confirms pulses only render when circuit.loads[0].state==='on'.
findings.verify_reason: The code matches the claim: dots appear after time>35 without a connection, start at Pip (not at the plug while !holdingPlug), and use detour() with only this.obstacles, the two pillars (src/game.ts:446). The specific shot-33 claim is overstated. From spawn the straight line misses the crate stack near Pip (the dots pass behind it). The nearest props to that line are a crate at (1.4,-2.05) at 0.35 m (edge-touching) and a bookshelf at (1.95,-1.4) at 0.5 m, which the line most likely crosses. From the back wall (-1.4,-8) the line passes a bookshelf at (-1.42,-8.37) at 0.37 m, so it goes through it. The 'teaches flow-out misconception' point is a design argument, not a demonstrated harm, and the hint only appears for idle players. Downgraded to P2.

findings.title: The reel has no visible source, so the 'loop' the room teaches is not truthful or readable
findings.problem: The anchor reel at (-8,4) is a free-standing spool on an ink base plate (src/game.ts:89-91), 2 m from the side wall, with nothing connecting it to a wall outlet or supply. The practice wall of five sockets is on the back wall, far away and unconnected (src/levels/decor.ts:96-97). The level is meant to teach that a switch closes the loop (research-docs 1.2), but the scene shows electricity appearing from an unplugged reel and ending at a lamp, with no source and no return. That breaks AGENTS 10 (electricity truthful at the level taught). It is also a missed play-by-doing beat: the first room could show 'source → cable → switch → lamp' as physical objects. The how-to poster (decor.ts:98-104) shows reel → plug → socket → lamp and also omits the source and the switch.
findings.fix: In src/levels/decor.ts playground() (or next to the anchor build in game.ts:89), add a wall outlet plate on the side wall at (-10,·,4) and a short fixed lead from the reel's hub to it, drawn with hoseGeometry or a TubeGeometry in the cable's white. Give the outlet a small green 'live' pip. Update the howto glyph to show outlet → reel → plug → socket → switch → lamp. Optionally pulse the reel's hub light once the loop closes, to show that both ends matter.
findings.verify: Start shot plus a zoom-9 crop of the reel: a lead to a wall outlet is visible. Retake the how-to poster crop.
findings.verify_reason: The anchor at src/game.ts:89-91 is two spools, a hub and an ink base plate, with no lead to any outlet. The practice sockets on the back wall (decor.ts:96-97) are unconnected. The how-to glyph (decor.ts:98-104) shows reel → plug → socket → lamp with no source and no switch. The first room depicts power coming from an unplugged reel, which conflicts with the truthful-electricity hard rule. The 'no return' part is not a real problem: a two-core cable carries its return.
findings.fix_correction: Drop the 'no return' argument. A lead from the reel to a wall outlet is enough at this level.

findings.title: False affordances: a second cable reel, a job-yellow splitter, cage reels and a glowing practice socket look like job items
findings.problem: The card says 'Pick up the reel's plug' and then 'lamp's socket'. The room also offers: (1) the `parts` clutter recipe (src/levels/playground.ts:5 → src/levels/clutter.ts:44), which places a grabbable kind:'reel' at (-4.51,-8.93) whose prompt reads 'E Grab the cable reel', and a splitter at (-3.81,-8.53) in the exact job yellow #ffc94d (prefabs.ts:24) with the prompt 'E Grab the splitter' (shot 37). Carried to the socket, the splitter just sits on the socket box and nothing happens (shot 38). (2) A yellow #ffc94d and a red reel inside the supply cage (src/levels/decor.ts:108-113), right next to the start and in the first frame (shots 01, 05). (3) The practice wall of five sockets on the back wall, where the middle one carries a green glow (decor.ts:96-97). It is the most 'live'-looking socket in the room and catches the eye in every back-wall view (shots 13, 32, 37). The real socket is an unlit dark box. A new player reading 'reel' and 'socket' has several wrong candidates, and the real lamp socket is the least prominent one.
findings.fix: Remove 'parts' from the playground recipes (playground.ts:5), or add a clutter option that excludes kind reel/splitter on cable floors. Recolour the cage's decorative reels to a neutral grey/kraft (decor.ts:110, replacing '#ffc94d' with '#b9b2a4'), or remove them. Drop the green glow on the practice socket (decor.ts:97), and instead give the real lamp socket (decor.ts:92 rbox) a teal emissive face plus the pulsing ring it already has. Make the real socket box a lighter outlined plate rather than #384454 on the dark base.
findings.verify: In the start, survey and back-wall shots, count reel- or splitter-like props and glowing sockets that are not job items. The target is 0 (DR-17). The prompt near (-4.5,-8.9) never says 'cable reel'.
findings.verify_reason: The props dump shows a reel at (-4.51,-8.93) and a splitter at (-3.81,-8.53) from the 'parts' recipe. NAMES gives the prompts 'cable reel' and 'splitter', and shot 37 shows 'E Grab the splitter'. One correction: the decoy reel is kraft #c98f5a (the recipe's pick() colour), not job yellow. The splitter has no colour, so it falls back to the job yellow #ffc94d. The cage reels are #ffc94d and #e5484d (decor.ts:113), and the green glow on the middle practice socket shows in shots 13, 32 and 37. I did not verify the 'splitter sits on the socket' outcome.
extra_evidence: v2.mjs a / v1.mjs decoys: reel color #c98f5a, splitter color undefined → prefab #ffc94d (src/props/prefabs.ts:24)

findings.title: Bookshelves and other tall clutter hide Pip; only pillars fade
findings.problem: The occlusion fade raycasts camera → Pip (y+0.4) against `occluders`, which only holds pillars and interior walls (src/game.ts:387-388, src/levels/decor.ts:55-57). The playground's `shelf` recipe puts five 2 m × 1.8 m bookshelves (prefabs.ts:20, mass 24) in the middle and along the back of the room (positions from the props dump: (1.95,-1.4), (4.47,1.07), (-3.64,-6.52), (-1.42,-8.37), (4.01,-8.66)). At the default camera they cover Pip entirely: in shot 37 only Pip's hat shows over the shelf near the back wall, and in shot 45 Pip's body is hidden behind the shelf at (4.47,1.07). These shelves sit beside the clean route and the back-wall approach to the lamp, and the cable vanishes behind them too.
findings.fix: In Game.addProp (src/game.ts:116), for prefabs with size[1]≥1.2 (bookshelf, cabinet, cooler, vending, printer, whiteboard), give each a cloned transparent toon material and register its mesh parts as occluders. Because props are instanced in batchProps, either exclude tall kinds from batching or add a per-instance opacity attribute. Cast three rays (feet, chest y+0.9, head y+1.6) and fade to ≤0.25 within 0.2 s (lerp factor about 0.35 at 60 fps). Alternatively keep the shelf recipe against the walls only (fillBand) in playground.ts.
findings.verify: Repeat e-camera.mjs 'occ': stand at (4.4,0.35) and (-4.1,-7.8) and sweep 4 yaws. At least 70% of Pip's pixels stay visible in every shot (DR-12).
findings.verify_reason: Only pillar bodies (decor.ts:55) and game.box(fade) meshes are pushed to occluders, and the raycast at game.ts:387-388 checks only those. In shot 37 only Pip's hat shows over the back-wall shelf at (-1.42,-8.37). In shot 45 Pip's body is behind the shelf at (4.47,1.07). The props dump confirms all five bookshelves at the cited positions.

findings.title: The clean run is a 5-second walk with no comedy, and the slingshot never surfaces
findings.problem: Replaying the spec route (b-clean.mjs) wins at t=4.98 s, with damage 0, alarmed 0 and fastestProp 0 throughout. Peak strain was 0.908 at the socket, so the 'Q Let go to slingshot the cable' prompt (src/ui/objectives.ts:79, strain>.97) never appears. Nothing is bumped, no coworker reacts, and the cable never turns red. The clutter lanes (playground.ts:6) deliberately keep the clean route clear, and the reel is 19 m against an 18 m straight-line distance, so length never pushes back. The Good Job signature (electronics as slingshots, AGENTS 4) and the pins exist, but a new player who does the task well finishes the first room without discovering either. DR-03 fails: nothing funny happens in the first 30 s unless the player goes looking. The tutorial teaches F, walk, F, E, but not cable feel.
findings.fix: Make the clean route brush the limit once. Either shorten the reel to about 16.5 m (playground.ts:6 length), so the direct line overstretches and the player must route around pillar-a's west side (the spec route, which still reaches at about 0.97), or move the socket to (8,-7.5). Put a light, unbreakable, funny prop cluster (a cone stack, or a trainee holding a paper stack) on the clean route's last bend, so the taut cable sweeps it and a coworker shouts '!'. Add a one-time hint: the first time strain passes 0.9, flash the red end of the cable and play the twang, so the player learns the colour language. Keep the slingshot optional.
findings.verify: Rerun b-clean.mjs. Max strain is ≥0.97 at least once, alarmed ≥1 or fastestProp >2 before t=30 (DR-03), and the routes.spec playground test still passes within 20 s.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced the spec route: max strain while walking was 0.914, damage 0, alarmed 0, fastestProp 0, bends 1. On plug-in the rope reads 18.4 m, strain 0.968, so the Q/slingshot prompt never appears. However, the proposed 16.5 m reel is technically wrong. The spec route needs 18.4 m once plugged, so at 16.5 m it would sit at strain 1.115, at the edge of the plug-in snap limit (<1.12), and Pip cannot drag much past the length (the pull force caps it). The route would not 'still reach at about 0.97'. That would break tests/routes.spec.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-playground-play/v1.mjs: leg3 strain .914 len 17.36 bends 1; plugged len 18.4 strain .968; dmg 0 alarmed 0
findings.fix_correction: Shorten the reel to about 18.7–18.8 m, so the spec route ends at strain ≈0.98–0.99 (red jitter and twang while still pluggable), or keep 19 m and move the socket about 0.5 m further. Do not go to 16.5 m. Keep the bump-a-funny-prop cluster light and optional: the clean route must still complete with 0 damage, per the clean-first and never-fail-for-chaos rules.

findings.title: The pins are hard to slingshot on purpose but trivial to walk through, so the strike rewards walking, not the cable
findings.problem: The pins (src/levels/playground.ts:18) sit in a cleared lane at x 4.4–5.5, z 4.7–5.9. slingshot() (src/game.ts:255-258) only flings props within 1.1 m of the rope polyline, and pushes them radially away from the reel. In testing: the spec slingshot flung the crate row but knocked down 0 pins (c-chaos 1). Overstretching south from (9,3.7), and south-east from (8.6,6.6), also knocked down 0 pins (d-wrong pins S/SD). A deliberate loop south of the pins and back up the east side, then a sprint and Q, knocked all 6 (f-aim 'behind'), but nothing in the scene suggests that loop. Meanwhile, walking or dragging the cable along the lane to (9,5.2) knocked all 6 on the way (d-wrong 'frontlane', pins 6 on arrival), and walking through the triangle knocked 3 (shot 28). pinsDown also counts a pin that only slid 0.5 m (game.ts:252-253). The bonus meant to showcase the slingshot (PROGRESS 'pins to fling at') is earned by bumping into it.
findings.fix: Make the slingshot the natural way to strike. (1) Move the pins so the taut cable crosses them on an obvious overstretch line. For example, put the triangle at x 0.5–1.6, z 7.6–8.8 (south of the crate row, which the clutter fill keeps clear), and add a 'bowling lane' floor decal from the reel side toward it. Then running east from the reel past its length lays the cable across the pins. (2) Protect them from walk-throughs: surround the triangle with a low, ankle-height rope barrier (fixed collider about 0.25 m high, which the rope ignores at y<1.8), or count a pin down only if it was hit while `flung` (set a flag in slingshot() for props it impulses). (3) Fire the strike confetti only for slingshot hits, and give a smaller 'bonk' for walk-ins.
findings.verify: New spec 'slingshot strikes the pins': F, sprint east past length, Q → pinsDown ≥4. Walking through the triangle at walk speed leaves pinsDown ≤1.
findings.verify_reason: I walked through the triangle without the plug, mostly at walk speed (hops under 2.5 m, so no sprint): pinsDown went from 0 to 6 and the strike confetti fired. In my screenshot most pins are still upright after only sliding. pinsDown (game.ts:252-253) counts slid >0.5 m as down, so the 'strike' can be earned with pins still standing. slingshot() pushes radially from the anchor, as cited. I did not reproduce the claim that the spec slingshot knocks 0 pins.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-playground-play-05-pins-walked.jpg (strike/confetti and 3 stars lit, pins mostly standing)
v2.mjs c: after walk-through (walk speed, no plug) pinsDown 6
findings.fix_correction: Also tighten pinsDown to tipped-only (up.y<0.7), dropping the 0.5 m slide rule, or require a slide of more than 1.2 m.

findings.title: The bonus goals are invisible during play: two stars are pre-lit, the stars are tiny, and the pause screen doesn't list them
findings.problem: The card shows three roughly 10 px stars with no text (src/ui/objectives.ts:108-115; zoomed crop shot 60). Two are gold from the first frame ('under 45 s' and 'break nothing' are true until broken), and the pins star is grey. A player reads this as 'already earned 2 of 3' or as a rating, not as goals. The code comment says 'their wording is on the pause and result screens' (objectives.ts:108-109), but the pause screen (shot 46, innerText dumped) shows only the title, tallies, buttons and key map, with no bonus text. The wording first appears on the result card (src/ui/game-ui.ts:216-217, shot 18), after the 5-second job is over. The bonus also says 'pins' while the in-world prompt says 'E Grab the cone' (NAMES cone:'cone', objectives.ts:57; shot 28), and the pins are modelled as white traffic cones. Nothing during play tells the player that knocking them over is a goal (DR-10, DR-50).
findings.fix: (1) Add the bonus list to pauseMarkup (src/ui/screens.ts) via objectives.results(), as the comment promises. (2) Draw the stars hollow until a goal is actually secured, filling a star when the pins strike happens or at the result card, and make them at least 16 px. (3) Model the pins as bowling pins (white lathe profile with a red neck band) instead of cone prefabs. Add a 'pin' prop kind or a variant of 'cone', with NAMES pin:'pin', so the prompt says 'Grab the pin'. (4) Optionally put a small wordless pin-icon plaque by the lane.
findings.verify: Pause shot lists 3 bonus lines. Start-shot crop shows 3 hollow stars, each ≥16 px. The prompt by the triangle says 'pin'.
findings.verify_reason: Shot 46 (pause) has no bonus text, despite the objectives.ts:108-109 comment saying the wording is on the pause screen. Shot 60 shows one grey and two gold stars from frame one. The wording appears only on the result card (game-ui.ts:216-217, shot 18). The pins are cone prefabs, and the prompt says 'Grab the cone' (shot 28 and my shot 05).
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-playground-play-05-pins-walked.jpg prompt 'E Grab the cone' next to the pins

findings.title: Crates and other light props don't wrap the cable, so it clips through the 'obstacle course' and routing comes down to one pillar
findings.problem: simulateCable only counts props with mass ≥3 as rope corners (src/game.ts:273). Crates (box mass 2), cones (1), bins (0.5) and plants (2) (src/props/prefabs.ts:10-14) never wrap. The playground's 'obstacle course' is mostly crates (src/levels/playground.ts:9-12, comment 'crate stacks … to drag the cable through'). In play, the taut cable passes straight through the crate stack at (8.2–8.9, 8.2–8.4) (shots 30, 51, 61) and through crates near Pip. The clean route has exactly one bend (pillar-a) (b-clean log bends:1). Because the rope is a taut visibility string, Pip's walked path doesn't matter unless it goes round a heavy prop, so 'route and wrap' (AGENTS 4, the cable is the star) is a single decision. The visual clipping also breaks DR-73.
findings.fix: Lower the wrap threshold to mass ≥1.5 for props resting on the floor (y<0.8) in src/game.ts:273, so crates, plants and stacked boxes wrap. A crate can still be dragged by the strain impulse at game.ts:334, which gives the comedy of a cable hauling a crate round. Keep the 20-nearest cap for performance. Then rebuild the crate row and crate pile in playground.ts:11-12 as two deliberate 'chicanes' the clean route must go around, so the player makes two or three wrap decisions.
findings.verify: Close shot at the (8.2,8.3) stack while overstretched: the cable bends round the crate edge with no interpenetration. The b-clean log shows bends ≥2 on the clean route, and routes.spec playground still passes.
findings.verify_reason: simulateCable only takes props with mass>=3 as rope corners (src/game.ts:273), and box/plant/cone/bin masses are 2/2/1/0.5 (prefabs.ts:10-14). My clean run shows bends:1 (pillar-a only). Shot 51 shows the taut orange cable running into the crate pile beside Pip.

findings.title: The yellow wall lines mislead: following them runs out of cable 5 m short, and the only prompt then says 'slingshot'
findings.problem: The decor comment says 'Painted lane lines lead from the reel to the lamp socket' (src/levels/decor.ts:85). The lines actually form a U around three walls (z=5.8 full width, x=-9.6, z=-8.2), about 30 m, against a 19 m reel (decor.ts:86). They are the most prominent floor guides in the start view (shot 01) and look like a path. Following them with the plug (d-wrong lane), Pip stalls at (2.02,-6.29), 5 m short of the socket, at strain 1.014. Sprinting the back way stalls 2.99 m short at strain 1.045 (g-misc). At that moment, the key cable-length lesson, the only guidance is the prompt 'Q Let go to slingshot the cable' (src/ui/objectives.ts:79). That suggests a chaos action that drops the plug further from the goal, rather than the real fix (go back and take a shorter line). Pressing F there also slingshots, since releasePlug fires at energy>1 (game.ts:261): 20 m/s props, damage 2.
findings.fix: (1) Repaint the floor guide along the real clean route: a dashed yellow line on the lanes[0] polyline from playground.ts:6 ((-7,5)→(-5,-1)→(-4,-4)→(5.8,-5.5)), ending in a socket icon. Keep the perimeter lines as thin grey hazard edges, or remove them. (2) In promptFor (objectives.ts:79), when strain>1 and the plug is more than 2 m from the target, show {key:'Q',text:'Let go'} without the word 'slingshot'. Show the slingshot wording only when a prop lies within 1.1 m of the rope. (3) Have the HUD reel meter (game-ui.ts updateStrain) flash its empty state with a short 'boing' when length is exhausted, as a wordless 'out of cable' cue.
findings.verify: Run d-wrong.mjs lane: the painted line leads to the socket within reel length. At the stall point the prompt does not say slingshot. Retake shot 32.
findings.verify_reason: decor.ts:85-86 has the comment 'lead from the reel to the lamp socket', but it draws three full-length lines: z=5.8 and z=-8.2 across the whole width, plus x=-9.6. That is a U of about 30 m around the room, and none of it ends at the socket (7,-6). Shot 32 shows the stall on the back line at red strain with the only prompt 'Q Let go to slingshot the cable'. releasePlug slingshots at energy>1 (game.ts:259-262).

findings.title: Phone 390×844: the survey crops off the lamp and the job card covers the cable strain meter
findings.problem: At 390×844 the survey (Tab, fixed zoom 44, src/game.ts:366) shows only the left two-thirds of the room (shot 49). The lamp, socket and east wall (x>5) are off-screen, and the prompt pill sits over the front of the room. Survey exists to find the goal, so on a phone it fails (DR-21). While dragging (shot 50), the two-line objective card ('Drag the cable to the lamp's socket and plug it in') overlaps the top-right strain/reel meter: only the reel icon edge and the end of the bar peek out. That meter is the HUD read of cable state (DR-46), and the spool on the reel is off-frame mid-drag (shot 56). The thumbstick, plug and grab buttons also cover the bottom third, where the cable trails.

findings.title: Grading is untuned: default limits give AAA in 5 s and wrecking still earns an A
findings.problem: The playground passes no limits, so grade() uses 120 s / 10 damage / 300 cost (src/sim/grade.ts:3). The clean run takes 4.98 s (b-clean), 24× under the time limit. 'Finish in under 45 seconds' (objectives.ts:28) is unmissable, and the result card shows A/A/A with the time row highlighted (shot 18). With overall = best of three, pure wrecking (more than 10 breaks) still gets A from time and cost, so the grade carries no information and gives no reason to replay (DR-07).
findings.fix: Add level-level limits (types.ts Level.limits?) and pass them in Game.win (game.ts:354): playground {time:15, damage:3, cost:40}. Change the time bonus to 'Finish in under 12 seconds'. Consider letting the result card name the axis that earned the grade.
findings.verify: Unit test in grade.test.ts for the playground limits. b-clean finishes as A (about 5–8 s), and a run with 12 breaks shows damage C.
findings.verify_reason: grade.ts:3 defaults to 120/10/300, and overall=[...parts].sort()[0] is the best of the three letters, so a fast run with heavy wreckage still gets A. Shot 18 shows A/A/A at 0:04. The playground passes no limits to grade().

findings.title: 'Q Let go to slingshot' shows at strain 0.97, but nothing slingshots below about 1.007
findings.problem: The prompt and the Q button's 'ready' glow turn on at strain >0.97 (src/ui/objectives.ts:79, src/ui/game-ui.ts throw.ready). Rope energy is (length−max)²×60 (src/sim/cable.ts:70), and releasePlug only slingshots when energy>1 (src/game.ts:261), which needs about 0.13 m of overstretch: strain ≈1.007 on the 19 m reel. Between 0.97 and 1.007 (e.g. the 'aim-around' run reached 0.998 and showed the prompt), Q just drops the plug with a thud. The prompt promises an action the key does not perform (DR-19).
evidence: mockups/review5/tools/playground-play/f-aim.mjs (log aim-around stretched strain .998, Q → pins 0, fast .01)
findings.fix: Gate the prompt and button on g.rope.energy>1 (or strain>1+0.13/maxLength) instead of strain>.97. Keep the red colour and jitter at 0.97 as a warning.
findings.verify: At strain 0.98 the prompt reads 'F Drop the plug'; at 1.02 it reads the slingshot line, and Q moves a prop (fastestProp>2).
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced. At strain 0.990 (length 18.82 m) the prompt read 'Q Let go to slingshot the cable' and the throw button had 'ready'. Pressing Q released the plug with fastestProp 0.00: nothing flew. Energy=(over)²·60 needs about 0.13 m of overstretch (strain ≈1.007) to exceed 1 (cable.ts:71, game.ts:261).
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-playground-play/v2.mjs d: pt 8.4,-3.6 strain .973 prompt slingshot throw:R; Q at .990 -> fastestProp 0.00

findings.title: A faded pillar leaves its cap, base and rail opaque, floating like a tabletop
findings.problem: pillar() fades only the 3 m body mesh on game.root (src/levels/decor.ts:55). The base trim, the 0.12 m cap at y 3.02 and the rail at 1.06 go on decorRoot (decor.ts:56) and stay fully opaque. When Pip walks behind pillar-b, the striped body goes ghostly while an orange slab hangs in mid-air over Pip and a brown base slab sits on the floor (shots 40, 41). It reads as a floating table, and the ghost stripes still cover Pip at opacity 0.15 (DR-78).
findings.fix: In pillar() put the cap, base and rail on game.root with cloned transparent materials, push them to game.occluders, and fade them together. Or parent them to the faded body so the existing fade loop (game.ts:388) drives the whole group. Consider fading to 0.1 with alphaHash to avoid sorting ghosts.
findings.verify: Retake shot 41 (zoom 9 behind pillar-b): no opaque slab floats above Pip.
findings.verify_reason: In pillar() (decor.ts:55-56) only the body mesh goes to game.root/occluders. Base, cap and rail go on decorRoot and stay opaque. Shot 41 shows the ghosted striped body with an opaque orange cap slab floating above Pip and the base slab on the floor.

findings.title: Draw calls of 700–970 at the game camera are 3–4× the 250 budget
findings.problem: snapshot().drawCalls reads 695–886 during play and 970 on the win frame (b-clean, c-chaos logs) for a 109-prop room, against the DR-24 budget of about 250. notes.fun: What works: the cable itself is a joy. Strain reads white → yellow → orange → red along its length, with jitter, twang arcs and a buzz at the limit (shots 13, 22, 23), and the overstretched slingshot launches the crate row with shake and sound (shots 24–25). Coworkers pop '!' when a taut cable sweeps past them or a crate lands nearby (shots 30, 54). Pip can topple a 24 kg bookshelf by walking into it, and the win beat (bloom on the lamp, confetti, Pip cheering, the rising result tag) is warm (shots 16–17). What doesn't: the room's best toys are hidden from someone who just does the task. The clean spec route wins in 4.98 s with zero props moved and peak strain 0.91, so the Q prompt never appears. The pins, the advertised slingshot target, were knocked down in 0 of 5 straight slingshot attempts but fall over when you walk or drag the cable through them (they sit on the open lane), so the strike doesn't reward the cable. Grading (default 120/10/300) hands out AAA for anything. Crates don't wrap the cable, so the 'obstacle course' is decoration and routing is one pillar decision. Net: fun if you go looking, flat if you follow the card.
notes.playability: No soft-locks found. Every run reached its end state, and all scripts closed with zero console or page errors (DR-80 pass). The plug can always be re-picked within 1.75 m (dropped mid-route, after a slingshot, at the room's front lip), plug-in snaps from 1.6 m with a clear 'F Plug in' and a ready-glow on the F button, and the switch can be pressed before power (it latches, so plugging in later wins at once). Problems: tall clutter, especially the five 1.8 m bookshelves from the shelf recipe, hides Pip because only pillars fade (shots 37, 45). A faded pillar leaves an opaque cap floating over Pip (shot 41). Running into the crate/chair cluster with the plug stalls Pip and costs damage. On a phone the survey crops off the lamp and the card covers the strain meter (shots 49, 50). There is no dead time; the opposite problem is that the whole job lasts about 5 s. The desktop survey shows the whole room (shot 02, DR-21 pass at 16:10). Restart is a page reload with autostart.
notes.clarity: At start the card and prompt agree ('Pick up the reel's plug' / 'F Pick up the plug', DR-42 pass), with 9 words on screen (DR-40 pass), and the grab reticle and marker sit on the plug. After that, clarity drops. The lamp and socket are off-screen for most of the drag, with no edge indicator. The lamp is a low-contrast grey pole, while the brightest 'socket' in the room is a green-glowing decorative one on the practice wall. A second grabbable cable reel, a job-yellow splitter and yellow reels in the cage are false affordances. The yellow wall lines look like a path to the lamp but run 30 m round the walls, and following them strands Pip with only a 'slingshot' prompt. 'Switch the lamp on' points at a bare pole with no switch. The bonus goals are three roughly 10 px stars, two pre-lit, worded only on the result card (not on pause as the code comment says), and they call the white cones 'pins' while the prompt says 'cone'. The marker shares the lamp shade's yellow and reads as its light beam.
notes.teaching: The room aims to teach cable feel (length, wrap, strain) and that a switch closes a loop. Cable feel is partly taught. Strain colour, the HUD reel bar and the pull-back are clear when you reach the limit, but the clean route never reaches it, and light props don't wrap, so length and route lessons are thin. The loop is not taught at all: the reel isn't connected to any source, the lamp has no visible switch, and nothing shows open vs closed beyond the final light-up. The idle hint (35 s) streams cyan 'current-like' dots from Pip to the socket on an open circuit, the misconception the game should avoid, and the dots run through crates. Truthful parts: the cable turns gold and pulses only once the lamp is actually on; the lamp only lights with both plug and switch; F at the socket requires the plug to be near.
notes.models: Within this dimension: the lamp now has a pole, arm, shade and bulb that blooms (the R2 'black bowling ball' is fixed), but it lacks a switch and reads small and grey from the game camera. The socket is a plain dark box. The pins are modelled as white traffic cones, not bowling pins. The hazard pillars are clean. Kraft beanbags still read as bread loaves (P5 still open, shots 01, 05). The floor remains bright: about 194–207 luma in the start shot, above the 140–185 target (DR-54 still failing). The cable clips through crates (light props don't wrap) and enters Pip through the legs from behind (P3 still open).
